title: Swap Lab Phase 2b research: engine thermal model and 3-minute sustained drift-session heat-soak test
brief: scratchpad research-brief.md (Phase 2, part 2b); CLAUDE.md rules 2 and 13
scope: Energy balance at full load (SI piston, turbo vs NA, heat to oil), rotary (Wankel) heat rejection, radiator / oil-cooler / intercooler capacity, fans, thermal mass and fluid properties, coolant and oil capacities for SR20DET, 2JZ-GTE, 13B-REW, VQ35DE, VQ35HR, M54B30, S54B32, safe temperature limits, and drift-session reality.
method: Primary documents were preferred: factory workshop/service manuals, owner's manuals, BMW technical training, Toyota New Car Features, Mazda (Toyo Kogyo) engineering books, NASA contractor reports, US patents, a glycol maker's product guide, a cooler maker's rating chart and Formula DRIFT's 2026 regulations. Scanned pages were rendered locally and read on the page image; text layers were used where present. Chart values are marked as read from charts. Computations (unit conversions, boiling points from Antoine constants) are marked 'derived' or confidence 'estimated' with the method given. No terms of use, licence or download agreements were accepted, no account was created and nothing was logged into; blocked or gated pages are listed under 'gates'.

confidenceKey.verified: two independent sources agree, or one source plus an independent cross-check

accessedNote: Every source entry was read on 2026-09-30 unless it says otherwise (only 'tm-repo-engine-masses' points to older repo data).
keyNumbers: SI piston engine at maximum power: brake 25-28 %, coolant 17-26 %, exhaust 34-45 % of fuel energy (Heywood; eb-heywood-maxpower); oil about 2.5 % near full load (Porsche chart; eb-porsche-vs-bmep); oil about 12 % of coolant heat (Ford patent; eb-oil-share-piston).

Rotary (Mazda, full load 4000 rpm, lambda 0.95): brake 26, oil 7, water 12, exhaust 36, unburned 16, radiation 3 % (ro-mazda-heat-balance); oil about 58 % of water heat; coolant heat about 0.55-0.76 kW per kW output at WOT (ro-mazda-water-per-power).
Setrab oil coolers: 0.05-0.29 kW/K depending on size at 5-8 gpm and 60-80 mph (oc-setrab-ratings).
JZA80 factory radiators: 46-49 kW 'low-speed' and 83-92 kW 'high-speed' ratings (conditions unknown) (ra-jza80-toyota).
Radiator SD is independent of ambient 10-50 °C to within 2 % (ra-sd-temperature-independence); heat rejection rises 1.8-2.1x from 3 to 10 m/s air speed (ra-scirp-table1).
Coolant volumes: SR20DET 6.2-7.0 L, 2JZ-GTE 8.8-9.5 L, 13B-REW 8.8 L, VQ35DE 8.7 L, VQ35HR 9.0 L, M54 8.4 L, S54 6.7 or 10.7 L (conflict).
cp: 50 wt% glycol 3.66-3.72 kJ/kgK (80-100 °C), water 4.21, oil about 2.1, cast iron 0.46, aluminium 0.90.
Boiling (50 wt% glycol): 124.6-128.0 °C at Nissan's 78-98 kPa caps, 130.4-134.7 °C at Mazda's 113-142 kPa, 142 °C at 2 bar; about 8 °C lower with water only.
Oil: BMW S54 normal 80-120 °C, maximum 150 °C in performance driving (lim-oil-s54).

driftSessions.item: Engineering analog: the worst cooling case is near-full fuel flow at low airspeed on a hot day

sources.title: NASA CR-165399 'Study of Advanced Rotary Combustion Engines for Commuter Aircraft', M. Berkowitz, C. Jones, D. Myers, Curtiss-Wright Corporation, February 1983 (NASA NTRS)
sources.quote: During the take-off and climb phase of flight, the ability of the cooling system to reject heat and properly cool the engine is most critical. The engine is rejecting heat at close to its maximum rate (near full fuel flow) while the aircraft is at a relatively low air speed. Maximum coolant and oil temperatures will occur during this flight phase. ... Limiting oil and coolant temperatures will occur during hot day operation. The coolers will be sized to meet the hot day requirements.

driftSessions.note: Supports the shape of the 3-minute test (high load, low airspeed, hot ambient); the 3-minute length and 70-90 % load remain the build prompt's design choice, not sourced facts.
